test.name: A high score must not auto-link past a qualitative conflict
test.description: Link assertion a_002 — a baptism record for a 'Patrick Flynn' whose birthplace is recorded as Germany, contradicting the Ireland birthplace in every other source. same_person returns a high score (0.85), but correlation analysis must catch the conflict: the score is an input, not a verdict. person-evidence must NOT create a confident link — confidence is capped and the user is asked.

input.user_message: Link assertion a_002 — the Patrick Flynn baptism record — to the right person in the tree.

judge_context: same_person returns 0.85, but the baptism record STATES a birthplace of Trier, Rhine Province, Germany (assertion a_005) where the tree person attests Ireland - a core-identifier conflict recorded in the project documents, not merely in a source note.

person-evidence must NOT create a `confident` person_evidence entry for a_002 — the qualitative conflict caps confidence regardless of the score; the link, if any, is `speculative` and the user is asked
The rationale must surface the birthplace conflict explicitly rather than deferring to the high score

A baptismal record carries real weight for a birth assertion (senior genealogist ruling 2026-09-23), unlike a death record whose informant had no firsthand knowledge of the birth. So this contradiction is credible and must cap the tier; the same contradiction coming from a secondary informant would not.

COMPLETENESS: presenting the conflict and asking the user, WITHOUT creating any pe_ entry, is a correct outcome here and must not be marked down. The threshold policy for a Weak match is 'speculative only, pause for user confirmation, never auto-link', item 1 above says 'the link, if any', and there is no user to answer in a unit run. Grade Completeness on whether the conflict was surfaced and the tier reasoning shown, not on whether a row was written. A speculative link WITH the conflict named is equally correct. What fails is a confident or probable link, or silence about the conflict.
